newsitem.title: GERMANY: Unit sales double Gehe 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Unit sales double Gehe 1996 profits.

text.p: Europe's leading pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG on Monday said income from unit sales helped more than double its 1996 earnings while its sales rose 11.8 percent to 21.4 billion marks ($12.7 billion).

The Stuttgart-based group also vowed to complete its takeover of British chain Lloyds Chemists Plc by the end of April and said it may force small shareholders -- who now control less than 10 percent of the British firm -- to sell.
Gehe reported a 108 percent surge to 440 million marks in net profit for the year.
Of its pre-tax profit of 865.6 million marks, more than half was due to the sale of four small pharmaceuticals units and the creation of a joint venture with Schering involving Gehe unit Jenapharm.
Gehe said it would keep its basic dividend unchanged at one mark per share, but would also pay a special dividend of 30 pfennigs per share.
Gehe sold off Azupharma, Aliud Pharma, allphamed and Paris-based GNR-Pharma in 1996 as part of its strategy to step out of pharmaceutical production entirely and focus more on wholesale business.

Turning to Lloyd Chemists, which it acquired earlier this year after a protracted battle to take it over with Unichem Plc, Gehe said it expected the company to turn a profit on sales of some 1.7 billion marks this year.
The takeover price for all 100 percent of Lloyds was 684.6 million pounds sterling, Gehe said.

Decisions on whether to retain all of Lloyds' business would be taken later in the year Gehe said. Lloyds' various interests included a health food chain and veterinary medicine. ($ = 1.691 German Marks)
